LESSON: READING 8.2.1 READING SYLLABLES

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.2: Reading 8.2.1 Reading syllables
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 8.2.1 Reading syllables, part of Strand 8 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: How do we read these syllables? 2. How do we read three letter words?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 8.2.1 Reading syllables together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self -efficacy as learner reads syllables accurately.

● Learning to learn as learner persists and pursues to read syllables correctly.

Values:
● Unity: inclusion as learner with other chant rhymes on syllables in unison.

● Integrity as learner with others practices fairness taking turns while blending sounds and reading syllables.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Ethnic and racial relations as learner reads sounds and forms syllables collaboratively with others across ethnic borders.

Link to other Activity Areas:

Reading across all learning areas require blending of sounds and letter signs to form syllables, syllables to form words,

words to form sentences and later paragraphs. Syllables reading is necessary in all.
